description: Verify that DUT discards a UDP datagram whose Length field claims more bytes than the IP payload actually carries (RFC 768 'Fields' MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
If UDP.Length > (IP payload length), the datagram is internally inconsistent — the parser would walk past the end of the buffer. RFC 768 requires the receiver to drop it. (Note: this is the over-claim variant; under-claim is covered by DATAGRAMLENGTH_01.)

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: UDP datagram with Length field intentionally larger than the IP payload byte count

2. Observation:
   • DUT's upper-tester must NOT receive the datagram (UT-query confirms drop)

[Pass condition]
UT-query confirms DUT did not deliver the over-length UDP.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_wrong_receipt — DUT delivered the over-length UDP (parser tolerated buffer over-walk)
• Fail_timeout — UT-query never arrived (test infra issue)

verdicts.Pass: DUT discarded the over-length UDP — normal
verdicts.Fail_wrong_receipt: DUT received UDP with Length greater than actual IP payload
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No UT confirmation for over-length discard
